items.name: The Photograph
items.significance: A framed photograph behind the bar showing a woman who looks exactly like Mixie, standing in the Triangle Bar in what appears to be the 1930s or 1940s. The central investigative object of Season One.
items.description: A black-and-white photograph in a simple frame. The woman behind the bar is unmistakably Mixie — or someone who shares her face across decades.

items.name: The Guest Ledger
items.significance: A leather-bound guest register at the front desk, continuously maintained since 1910. Contains the names of every guest, including M. Quinn (1935-1942) whose handwriting matches Mixie's.
items.description: Heavy leather binding, hand-ruled pages, entries in dozens of different hands spanning over a century. Pages turn on their own during storms.

items.name: Mixie's Notebook / Novel
items.significance: Mixie's handwritten novel about a bartender at a time-shifting lodge — which turns out to be inherited memory. Earlier drafts from 1936, 1938, and 1942 exist in the same handwriting.
items.description: A worn notebook that Mixie carries and writes in during quiet moments. The novel she is writing has been written before, by women who shared her face.

items.name: The Piano
items.significance: An upright piano in the Triangle Bar that plays notes without being touched during storms. Music is a portal in the ROOM 33 universe.
items.description: A well-maintained upright piano. During storms, it produces melodies that no one is playing — songs from other eras that open emotional doorways.

items.name: The Mirror (Triangle Bar)
items.significance: An antique mirror at the bar's entrance that reflects everything a fraction of a second late. The lodge's most visible supernatural artifact and Siobhan's portal.
items.description: A large antique mirror with an ornate frame. Its delay is constant and measurable. During Episode 9, it becomes the medium through which Mixie encounters Siobhan.

items.name: The Room 33 Key (Skeleton Key)
items.significance: A brass skeleton key that Room 33 returns to Mixie in exchange for her letter. Tarnished, heavy, warm to the touch.
items.description: An old skeleton key, not a modern key. Tarnished brass. Warm when Mixie picks it up. It appeared under Room 33's door after she slid her letter in.

items.name: Flynn's Pocket Watch
items.significance: Flynn repairs watches as meditation. During storms, the parts in Owl cabin rearrange themselves — gears stack, springs coil, faces align.
items.description: A collection of watch parts and tools on Flynn's nightstand. His meditation practice. The parts self-assemble during storms.

items.name: Jauncey's Song: "The Sea That Held Her"
items.significance: Jauncey's original song, performed for the first time in the Season One finale. About Siobhan, about Mixie, about the lodge. The season's musical resolution.
items.description: A folk song that Jauncey has been composing for years, finally performed in Episode 10. It captures the lodge's truth in music.

items.name: The Foresters' Symbols
items.significance: Geometric compass roses and coded marks left throughout the lodge by the Foresters of the Eternal Compass (1935-1943).
items.description: Compass roses enclosed in circles, geometric patterns, and text in the Foresters' cipher. Bold in the basement, discreet elsewhere.

items.name: The Brass Bell
items.significance: A service bell at the front desk that rings without being struck during storms. One of the lodge's oldest artifacts.
items.description: A small brass service bell, tarnished with age. It rings on its own during storms — a single clear tone that carries through the lobby.

items.name: Tom's Tools & Cigar Box
items.significance: Tom's meticulously organized workshop and his cigar box of 37 objects found in the Great Room fireplace ash after storms.
items.description: A cedar cigar box containing 37 catalogued items: a 1911 penny, a 1930s button, a 1960s guitar pick, and a fragment of paper from Mixie's notebook that has not yet been torn.

items.name: The Foresters' Journal & Records
items.significance: Partial records from the Foresters found in a locked library cabinet: meeting minutes, ritual notes in coded language, correspondence about "the Threshold Project," and an unfinished 1943 letter.
items.description: Coded meeting minutes, ritual notes, membership ledger (containing "Callahan"), and a final letter that stops mid-sentence in 1943.

items.name: Abandoned Guest Belongings
items.significance: Suitcases and personal effects in the Lost and Found from guests who vanished — each tagged with name, date, and room number by Tom.
items.description: Shelves of suitcases, hat boxes, and personal items. A child's bear from 1952 with no registered child. An unsent letter to "Rosemary." The locked Voss steamer trunk.

items.name: The Unlabeled Bottle
items.significance: A bottle behind the bar with no label, containing a spirit of unknown provenance. Mixie pours from it instinctively for certain guests. The liquid level never seems to change.
items.description: A dark glass bottle with no label. The liquid inside is amber, aromatic, and slightly warm. Mixie reaches for it without thinking for certain guests.

items.name: The Library Clock / Grandfather Clock
items.significance: A clock whose ticking syncs with the boiler's rhythm and the waterways' pulse. Accelerates during storms.
items.description: A tall case clock with a brass pendulum. Its rhythm matches the boiler's and the waterways'. It speeds up during storms and slows in calm.

items.name: The Landscape Painting
items.significance: A painting above the Great Room fireplace showing the lodge and surrounding landscape. The scene shifts subtly between viewings.
items.description: An oil painting of the lodge from the forest's perspective. Attentive viewers notice the painted season does not always match the real one.

items.name: Amber's Photograph
items.significance: A second photograph discovered later in the series — connected to a guest from an earlier era. Details reserved for Season Two.
items.description: A photograph album in the Lost and Found containing images of the lodge from impossible angles — aerial views decades before drones, shots from inside walls.
